question: Where is the Radio Astronomy Centre of India located?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Udhagamandalam**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Radio Astronomy Centre** of India is located in **Udhagamandalam**, also known as Ooty.
 
• It is one of the premier institutes for radio astronomy research in India.
 
• The centre operates under the **National Centre for Radio Astrophysics (NCRA)**, which is a part of the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR).
 
• The observatory is equipped with the **Ooty Radio Telescope (ORT)**, which is one of the largest radio telescopes in the world.
 
• The facility conducts research in various areas of radio astronomy including the study of pulsars, interstellar medium, and the cosmic microwave background radiation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Ooty Radio Telescope** was commissioned in **1970** and has been instrumental in numerous significant discoveries in the field of radio astronomy.
 
• Radio astronomy is a subfield of astronomy that studies celestial objects at radio frequencies.
 
• India has made significant contributions to radio astronomy, and the Radio Astronomy Centre in Udhagamandalam is a key institution in this field.
 
• Research conducted at the centre has implications for our understanding of the universe, including the study of cosmic phenomena such as black holes, neutron stars, and the large-scale structure of the cosmos.
